A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DeepResonance study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching relocated material from v1 Appendices A–H to v2 Appendices A–J.

before.justification: v1 reports original DeepResonance evaluations on six principal benchmarks, five zero-shot benchmarks, and component ablations, with detailed appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds backbone comparisons, caption-content ablations, and inference tests removing non-text modalities.

M1.justification: v2 adds Mistral-family and LLaMA-3 backbone variants of DeepResonance-α and β in Appendices G–H, extending model instantiations beyond Vicuna. The multi-sampled embeddings, fusion procedure, and two-stage training remain unchanged. Renaming the pre-alignment Transformer to pre-LLM fusion Transformer is terminological.

E1.justification: The training datasets, principal tasks, and zero-shot benchmarks are retained, as confirmed by v1 Table 4 and v2 Table 5. v2 adds a text-only inference scenario across the six principal tasks by removing music, image, and video inputs (Appendix D, Table 6), extending input-condition coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Tables 11–16 add NExT-GPT-Mistral and NExT-GPT-LLaMA-3 trained with Music4way as matched comparators for the corresponding DeepResonance variants. All original comparison methods remain; moving their descriptions to Appendix C does not remove them.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluation configurations using two 8B backbones, text-only inference controls, and training-target controls omitting visual captions or musical features. The original splits, metrics, epoch counts, learning rate, and batch size remain unchanged. No revised setting is stated to explain the changed original DeepResonance-α scores.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's instruction-data, embedding, and Transformer-depth ablations, v2 tests whether visual captions and musical features contribute through training targets (Table 4; Tables 22–24), whether predictions depend on non-text inputs (Table 6), and whether benefits transfer across backbones (Tables 11–16). These substantially broaden the diagnostic evidence about modality reliance and portability.

E5.justification: Appendix B in both versions reports means from three inference runs. Neither version adds seed information, confidence intervals, variability estimates, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 3 changes DeepResonance-α BLEU-1 from 44.6 to 48.7 on MI2T, 44.5 to 48.9 on MV2T, and 54.7 to 37.2 on Any2T, alongside other metric changes. The Any2T revision reverses its advantage over the retained MWIT-only result of 54.4 in the ablation tables. v2 also adds backbone and modality-ablation results; the five zero-shot result tables remain unchanged. The PDFs do not explain whether the revised α values are corrections or reflect unreported experimental changes.

T1.justification: Equations (1) and (2) and their mathematical definitions are retained. The Transformer rename does not change the formal model, and neither version supplies additional theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: music-centric multi-way datasets, multi-sampled embeddings and modality fusion, and superior performance across six music-understanding tasks. Additional experiments support these retained claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of caption-content contributions, non-text-input reliance, and why Vicuna may adapt more readily than other backbones (Section 5.5; Appendices D and G). It removes the Vicuna-only and MIR-feature-accuracy limitations and expands the rationale for random frame selection in short clips. The principal α/β applicability tradeoff remains.

D1.justification: v2 identifies the additional checkpoints as LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct and Ministral-8B-Instruct-2410 in Appendix G and documents the new ablation manipulations. It removes v1's direct M2UGen repository footnote. Existing optimization, hardware, runtime, and prompting details remain, and both versions describe releasing their own models and datasets as a future plan.

R1.justification: v2 adds Dubey et al.'s LLaMA 3 work and Jiang et al.'s Mistral 7B work in connection with the additional backbone evaluations. The broader related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 consistently renames the fusion Transformer, condenses Section 5.1 by moving baseline descriptions to Appendix C, adds a sanity-check appendix, and expands several analytical paragraphs. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 4 and 6, expands six appendix result tables into backbone-specific blocks, and adds caption-ablation blocks to three tables. Figure 2 is redrawn to show interleaved inputs explicitly, while Figures 1 and 5 receive updated graphics and labeling. Existing prompt/example tables are retained but redistributed. These constitute substantial changes to the presentation of evidence.

improvement.justification: Additional backbone comparisons address v1's explicit Vicuna-only limitation, while input and caption-content ablations make modality contributions more directly assessable. These provide a limited net improvement in validation. The gains are tempered by unexplained α-score revisions, Appendix D's overstated description of performance degradation despite MusicQA BLEU-1 increasing without music, and an inconsistency between Tables 4 and 24: β without musical features has Music4way-MusicCaps ROUGE-L of 48.0 versus 47.5.
